title: Viewing and Managing Data Inventory Details

blocks.text: DSPM scans various data stores to discover and classify sensitive data. After the scan completes, the discovered findings are aggregated and displayed in the Data Inventory. The Data Inventory page provides a unified view of files and database tables that contain sensitive data across cloud, SaaS, and on-premises environments. You can gain visibility into sensitive data stored in different locations, entities that have access to sensitive data, and how to investigate it further to reduce security risks and prioritize remediation.
To view the file or table details:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Data Security > DSPM > Data Inventory.
Click the File or Table Name to view the following tabs and actions:
Some columns contain service-specific data and might be empty when there is no relevant data.
Details
View the file or table properties.
See image.
Data Duplications
View duplicate copies of the file or table based on matching hash values. This allows you to delete duplicate copies containing sensitive data.
See image.
Click the required File Path to view the Details tab.
Click the required Data Store to view the Data Inventory graph.
Entitlements
This tab is available only for files, and additional details are shown only for on-premises SMB file shares.
View the list of users, computer accounts, and groups that have access to the files along with their roles and permissions.
See image.
Click a specific entity to view additional entitlement analysis details.
See image.
Evidence

Review the collected evidence to confirm that sensitive data exists. This tab is displayed only if evidence collection is enabled and configured prior to the scan. To learn more, see About Evidence Settings.
See image.
File Activity
This tab is available only for files.
View activities related to file labeling, the entity performing the action (e.g., Zscaler), and the timestamp.
Data

This tab is available only for tables and is currently supported for managed and unmanaged SQL databases, data warehouses such as Databricks and Snowflake, and NoSQL databases such as DynamoDB and CosmosDB. AWS DynamoDB tables do not support column-level scanning.
View database columns that contain sensitive data, precisely matching the data type with the specific column in the table.
See image.
Actions
Manually apply a Microsoft Information Protection (MIP) label to a file stored in on-premises file shares created on file servers and Azure file shares.
See image.
Some columns are shown for both files and tables and some are specific to files or tables:
Common for Both Types
Path: The file's location or absolute path to the table.
Resource Name: The name of the resource that contains the file or table.
Resource Type: The type of resource (e.g., AWS Bedrock Agent, AWS ECR Repository, Azure AI Foundry Hub) that contains the file or table.
Account: The cloud account ID where the file or table is stored.
DLP Engines: The DLP engines that match the sensitive data in the file or table.
DLP Dictionaries: The DLP dictionaries within the matched DLP engines.
Label: The sensitivity label (e.g., MIP label) applied to the file.
Hash: The hash value that uniquely identifies the file or table. Identical files have the same hash value.
Last Modified Time: The date and time the file or table was last modified.
File
Actions: The actions (i.e., Apply MIP Label) you can perform on the file.
Document Categories: The document categories (e.g., DMV, Financial, HR) to which the file belongs.
Document Types: The type of document.
Size: The size of the file.
File Type: The file extension.
File ID: The unique identifier of the file.
Resource Category: The resource category (e.g., Compute, Database) that contains the file.
Severity of Last Incident: The severity (i.e., High, Medium, Low) assigned to the most recent policy violation detected for this file.
Owner: The email address of the user who owns or is recorded as owning the file.
Last Scan Time: The date and time the file was last scanned.
File MD5: The MD5 hash value of the file.
Collaboration Scope: Whether the file has private or public access.
Public URL: The public URL to access the file.
Number of Internal Collaborations: The number of internal users who have access to the file.
Number of External Collaborations: The number of external users who have access to the file.
Internal Collaborator: The internal users having access to the file.
External Collaborator: The external users having access to the file.
Last Shared Users: The user who most recently shared the file.
Last Shared On: The date and time when the file was most recently shared.

blocks.heading: Manually Applying a MIP Label to Files

blocks.text: You can manually apply a MIP label to a single file or to multiple files stored in on-premises file shares created on file servers, or in Azure file shares. You must have the required permission to apply MIP labels. To learn more, see Predefined DSPM Roles and Permissions.
Before you apply a MIP label to a file in an Azure file share, make sure M365 tenant sync is enabled. To learn more, see Onboarding a Microsoft 365 Tenant

blocks.item: Apply a MIP Label to a Single File
To apply an MIP label to a single file:
Click the file that you want to label on the Data Inventory page or on the Sensitive Data tab of the Resource Inventory page.
The file details page appears.
On the Details tab, click the Actions drop-down menu.
See image.
Alternatively, click the Actions icon () for the required file in the Actions column.
See image.
Select Apply MIP Labels.
The Apply Label window appears.
In the Apply Label window:
Apply Label: Select the MIP you want to apply.
For multiple M365 tenants, Azure file shares use labels associated with the corresponding tenant, while on-premises file shares use labels from all available M365 tenants.
Add Comment (optional): Enter a comment.
Click Apply Action.
See image.
A message appears indicating that the action is submitted successfully, and the label is applied within a few minutes.
Apply a MIP Label to Multiple Files
To apply an MIP label to multiple files:
Select the files you want to label on the Data Inventory page or on the Sensitive Data tab of the Resource Inventory page.
Click the Actions drop-down menu.
See image.
Select Apply MIP Labels.
The Apply Label (bulk action) window appears.
In the Apply Label (bulk action) window:
Apply Label: Select the MIP you want to apply.
For Azure file shares, only labels associated with the corresponding M365 tenant are available, while on-premises file shares show labels from all available M365 tenants.
Add Comment (optional): Enter a comment.
Click Apply Action.
See image.
A message appears indicating that the action is submitted successfully, and the label is applied within a few minutes.

blocks.text: To check whether the label is applied:

blocks.item: Click the file for which you applied the MIP label.
The file details page appears.
On the file details page, select the File Activity tab.
Check the status of the label action.
The status can be one of the following:
Completed: Indicates that the label is applied successfully
Failed: Indicates that the label is not applied.
Requested Action: Indicates that the label application is in progress.
